title: Wang et al. 2024 — Brain Treebank: Large-scale intracranial recordings from naturalistic language stimuli
description: The Brain Treebank is a large-scale dataset of intracranial (stereo-EEG) recordings from 10 epilepsy patients who watched Hollywood movies. Signals were sampled at 2048 Hz from 1,688 electrodes in total, across 26 movie trials and about 43 hours of data. The movie audio was transcribed with manually annotated word onsets, and each transcript was parsed into Universal Dependencies syntax trees. This makes the dataset a resource for studying the neural basis of naturalistic language. This record provides the data in BIDS-iEEG format.
methods_description: Intracranial EEG was recorded at 2048 Hz from epilepsy patients undergoing clinical monitoring at Boston Children's Hospital while they passively watched Hollywood movies. Movie audio was transcribed, word onsets were manually annotated, and transcripts were parsed into Universal Dependencies trees. Per-trial HDF5 files were converted to BIDS-iEEG BrainVision format, with each movie as one run and corrupted electrodes flagged as bad.
